2196.note: AGS Estado 3591 f.181 no.2 (cipher chapter from Turin) is an eight-line cipher with a line of small cursive written over each line and struck through in ink, and f.183 is a clean copy headed 'Cap. de la carta descifrada de Turin' with the Spanish plaintext, so a contemporary decipherment sits with the cipher (images viewed on PARES).

seen.where: PARES, Archivo General de Simancas: https://pares.cultura.gob.es/ParesBusquedas20/catalogo/description/6174713 (EST,LEG,3591,181,2; 4 images) and https://pares.cultura.gob.es/ParesBusquedas20/catalogo/description/3681402 (EST,LEG,3591,183; 4 images); all eight images fetched with ViewImage.do (zoom 10) and viewed on 4 Nov 2026. The Melo covering letters (ff. 176-177) were not opened.
seen.extent: 181,2: image 1 carries about eight lines of cipher (numbers, letters and signs, roughly 90 groups); images 2-4 are blank or show only bleed-through. 183: image 1 carries seven lines of clear Spanish; images 2-4 blank.
seen.cipher: PARES title of 181,2: 'Capitulo cifrado de carta proveniente de Turin con impresiones del rey de Francia ante la llegada a ...'; title of 183: 'Capitulo de carta proveniente de Turin con impresiones del rey de Francia ante la llegada a Italia d...'. On the images: 181,2 has a clear heading 'Capitulo de [cipher] de Turin' and eight cipher lines, each with a line of small cursive written above it and then cancelled with a thick ink stroke (an interlinear decipherment, struck out); 183 is headed 'Capo de la carta descifrada de Turin' and begins 'El Rey de Francia ha escrito a Madama que ...'. So a decipherment is written on the cipher leaf and again as a clean 'descifrada' copy.
